ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an operational amplifier weighted inverting summing circuit. On the left side there are two input terminals A and B, labeled uI1 and uI2 respectively; uI1 is connected through resistor R1 to the common node near the op-amp inverting input terminal, and uI2 is also connected through resistor R2 to the same common node. The feedback resistor RF is connected back from the output terminal uO to this common node. The non-inverting input terminal of the op-amp is grounded through resistor R. Therefore this circuit is an ideal op-amp negative feedback structure, with the inverting terminal as the summing node and the non-inverting terminal grounded. Reasoning calculation: An ideal op-amp under negative feedback has virtual short and virtual open. The non-inverting terminal is grounded, so the potential of the inverting input node is approximately 0 V, that is, virtual ground. Write KCL for the inverting input node: uO = -RF * (uI1/R1 + uI2/R2). Substitute R1 = 10 kΩ, R2 = 20 kΩ, RF = 100 kΩ, uI1 = 0.2 V, uI2 = -0.5 V: uI1/R1 = 0.2/10k = 20 μA; uI2/R2 = -0.5/20k = -25 μA; the sum of the two is -5 μA. Therefore uO = -100kΩ * (-5 μA) = 0.5 V.

Treat the op-amp as ideal with negative feedback, set the inverting node to virtual ground, write KCL at that node, and solve uO = -100k*(0.2/10k + (-0.5)/20k) = 0.5 V.
